title: Make alternatives, with checked prices | 50agents
description: Make alternatives: n8n for long scenarios, Activepieces for a flat bill, Zapier for more apps, and 50agents to build from plain words. Prices checked.
answer: If Make's credits run out because every module costs one, n8n charges one execution for a whole run, and Activepieces gives 10,000 credits for $20 a month flat.
If you need more apps than Make's 3,500+, Zapier lists 10,541+; if you are tired of building scenarios module by module, 50agents builds the automation from plain words.
ask: Set up an automation: every new Shopify order is added as a row to my Google Sheet with its items and total
lede: Make bills by credit, and on its pricing page most actions consume one, so every module adds to the cost of each run.

entries.suits: People who use Make for the usual jobs, a new order to a sheet or a new lead to Slack, and are tired of mapping fields by hand.
entries.limit: No canvas, no routers to drag, no iterators set by hand. If you tuned nested branches and error handlers yourself, Make still does that better.

entries.suits: Make users comfortable with a bit of JavaScript who run long scenarios. The canvas will feel familiar, and one run of the whole workflow is one execution.
entries.price: No free cloud plan. Starter: €20 a month billed yearly (2.5K executions)
entries.limit: No free cloud plan, and the cloud prices are in euros and billed yearly.

entries.suits: Teams who want the widest app coverage and a simpler, linear editor that more people on the team can follow.
entries.price: Free: 100 tasks a month. Professional: $19.99 a month billed yearly (750 tasks)
entries.limit: Zapier counts each action step as a task, so long multi-step work usually costs more than on Make.

entries.suits: Small teams who want a predictable bill: a flat price for up to 5 users, with the option to self-host later.
entries.price: Free: 1,000 credits, up to 5 users. Plus: $20 a month flat (10,000 credits)

entries.suits: Teams whose scenarios mostly move data between Outlook, SharePoint, Teams and Excel, where Microsoft's own connectors are deepest.
entries.price: Free for cloud flows with standard connectors. Premium: $15.00 per user a month, paid yearly
entries.limit: Non-Microsoft apps often need premium connectors, at $15 per user a month paid yearly.

entries.suits: Teams who started with Make's AI modules and found they want an AI agent with tools, not a fixed path.
entries.price: No free plan. Pro: $37 a month (20,000 credits)
entries.limit: There is no free plan: the 14-day trial needs a card and turns into a paid plan unless you cancel.

us: Most of your scenarios are simple and you would rather say them than build them.
The person who needs the automation is not the person who builds scenarios.
You want sends to customers to wait for your approval by default.
them: You build complex scenarios with routers, iterators and error handlers, and you like seeing them. Make's canvas is still the best place for that.
You have many scenarios saved as blueprints and a team that knows them. The migration cost is real.
Your apps are in Make's 3,500+ and not in the others'.

move.title: Export blueprints
move.body: In each scenario, export the blueprint (.json). It imports back into Make only, but it records every module, filter and mapping, which is what you rebuild from.

move.title: Find the credit-hungry scenarios
move.body: Open your usage, sort scenarios by credits used and start with the top three. They decide whether the move saves money.

move.title: Rebuild one and compare outputs
move.body: Describe the scenario to Captain as you would to a colleague, then check its test run against the last real bundle in Make's history.

move.title: Switch off in Make
move.body: Once a week of runs match, turn the scenario off in Make. Keep the blueprint.

faqs.a: For long scenarios, n8n, because it bills per run, not per module. For a small team, Activepieces is $20 a month flat for 10,000 credits. Both have limits, listed in the table.

faqs.q: Does Make have a free plan?
faqs.a: Yes: 1,000 credits a month. Its own comparison page says paid plans start at $9 a month for 10,000 credits (Core).

faqs.q: Can I move Make scenarios to another tool automatically?
faqs.a: No. Blueprints import only into Make. Every alternative means rebuilding, so start with the scenarios that cost the most.
